solution.quick: Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition decreases as the steric hindrance and +I effect of alkyl groups increase. Thus, the order is Butanone < Propanone < Propanal < Ethanal.
solution.concept: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition reactions due to steric and electronic reasons. Sterically, the presence of two relatively large substituents in ketones hinders the approach of nucleophile to carbonyl carbon than in aldehydes having only one such substituent. Electronically, two alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more effectively in ketones than one alkyl group does in aldehydes through inductive (+I) effect.

Step 1: Identify the compounds: (A) Ethanal (CH3CHO), (B) Propanone (CH3COCH3), (C) Propanal (CH3CH2CHO), (D) Butanone (CH3COC2H5).

Step 4: Compare propanone (B) and butanone (D). Butanone has a larger ethyl group causing more steric hindrance and stronger +I effect than two methyl groups in propanone. Order for ketones: Butanone < Propanone.
Step 5: Combine to get overall increasing sequence: Butanone < Propanone < Propanal < Ethanal, which corresponds to (D), (B), (C), (A).

questionText: Acidified potassium dichromate oxidizes sulphides ($S^{2-}$) to:

solution.quick: Acidified potassium dichromate oxidizes sulfide ions (S^2-) to elemental sulfur (S). Hence Option C is correct.
solution.concept: In acidic solution, potassium dichromate acts as a strong oxidizing agent: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \to 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$. It oxidizes $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ or sulfide ions to elemental sulfur: $3\text{S}^{2-} \to 3\text{S} + 6e^-$.
solution.step_by_step:
Step 1: Write the reduction half-reaction: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \to 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Step 2: Write the oxidation half-reaction: $3\text{S}^{2-} \to 3\text{S} + 6e^-$.
Step 3: Combine: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 3\text{S}^{2-} \to 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{S}(s) + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Step 4: The product formed from sulfide is elemental sulfur (S).
solution.detailed:
In acidic solution, potassium dichromate acts as a strong oxidizing agent. The overall ionic equation is:

Sulfide ($S^{2-}$) is oxidized to colloidal sulfur ($S$). Hence Option C is correct.
